# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

Auth via Supabase (dev-login mints real HS256 JWT for testing)."

  - task: "Upheld-report counter + Creator Support escalation ladder (uphold action, zero-tolerance, rehab clear)"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "backend/server.py"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
        -working: "NA"
        -agent: "main"
        -comment: "NEW. apply_upheld(prof, category, admin, reason, severe) increments profile.upheld_reports and auto-applies ladder: 1=reminder activity; 3=creator_safety_flag=true; 5=7-day suspension + rules_reaccept_required; 7=30-day suspension + final_warning; 10+=banned. Zero-tolerance (severe=true OR category in csam/underage) => banned + no_appeal=true immediately regardless of count. Wired via POST /api/admin/reports/{id}/action with action='uphold' (ActionIn now has optional severe:bool); sets report status='upheld'. New POST /api/admin/users/{handle}/clear-strikes (require_admin, super/co only): resets strikes/upheld_reports/creator_safety_flag/final_warning/banned (12-month rehab appeal); 403 if no_appeal set. admin_users list now returns upheld_reports, creator_safety_flag, no_appeal, final_warning. public_profile exposes creator_safety_flag. TEST: super admin admin@clanchat.app/ClanChatAdmin!2025 (also has require_mod). Register adults V (victim/reporter) and T (target). (1) V reports T 5 times (POST /api/report {target_type:'user', target_id:T_handle, category:'harassment'}) capturing report ids — actually create 5 separate reports (report endpoint may dedupe? if so, vary note). For each report, super POST /api/admin/reports/{id}/action {action:'uphold', reason:'x'} and check the returned upheld_reports increments 1..5 and stage at 3 mentions creator_safety, at 5 => 7-day suspension. (2) GET /api/admin/users?q=T -> T has upheld_reports=5, creator_safety_flag=true, suspended_until set. (3) GET /api/users/{T_handle} -> creator_safety_flag=true. (4) Zero-tolerance: register target T2; V reports T2 (category:'harassment'); super POST action {action:'uphold', severe:true} -> returns stage 'terminated_no_appeal', banned true; GET /api/admin/users?q=T2 -> banned true, no_appeal true. (5) clear-strikes: super POST /api/admin/users/{T_handle}/clear-strikes -> 200; GET users -> T upheld_reports=0, creator_safety_flag=false. (6) super POST /api/admin/users/{T2_handle}/clear-strikes -> 403 (no_appeal). (7) A moderator (make one) can POST uphold (require_mod) but clear-strikes -> 403 (require_admin). NOTE: If /api/report dedupes reports from same reporter+target, create reports from different reporters OR the endpoint may allow multiple — inspect and adapt; the KEY assertions are the counter increments and ladder stages via repeated uphold calls (you can also call uphold on the SAME report id repeatedly if needed to drive the counter, since apply_upheld just increments the target's counter)."

        -comment: "NEW. Registration default now 'free' (admins seeded 'verified'). role removal resets account_type='free'. account_type exposed in serializers (profile, post author, dm thread user, dm_history peer, activity actor_account_type). (B) CO-ADMIN DM GUARD: super admin profile field allow_coadmin_dms (default False), exposed in /api/me. POST /api/admin/settings/coadmin-dms {enabled} (super_admin only, 403 for co_admin). POST /api/admin/dm-access/request {handle} (require_admin; 400 if requester is super_admin; 404 no user; 400 if target not super_admin; dedupes pending) -> creates db.dm_access pending + activity to target. GET /api/admin/dm-access -> super sees requests targeting them {as_super:true, allow_coadmin_dms, requests[]}; co-admin sees own. POST /api/admin/dm-access/{req_id}/{approve|deny} (only target super admin; 403 else; 404 missing; 400 bad decision) sets status + unused grant. ENFORCEMENT: super_dm_access_ok(actor,target) gates admin_view_dms AND admin_investigate: if target is super_admin and actor is a different non-super (co_admin) -> allowed only if target.allow_coadmin_dms OR an approved+unused grant exists (grant consumed one-time). Else 403. TEST: super=admin@clanchat.app/ClanChatAdmin!2025. Register adults CO, NORMAL. Make CO a co_admin (super assign co_admin). (1) super POST /api/admin/users/{NORMAL}/account-type {account_type:'premium'} -> 200; GET /api/users/{NORMAL} -> account_type='premium'. (2) invalid type 'gold' -> 400. (3) nonexistent handle -> 404. (4) CO (co_admin) POST /api/admin/settings/coadmin-dms {enabled:true} -> 403 (super only). (5) super POST /api/admin/settings/coadmin-dms {enabled:false} -> 200. (6) CO POST /api/admin/dm-access/request {handle:<super handle>} -> 200 pending; GET /api/me super handle: find via super token GET /api/me. Added 4 REST endpoints (all auth-required): POST /api/call/ring {peer, room, media} — enforces SAME barriers as livekit token (404 if peer not found, 400 self-call, 403 blocked, 403 adult_minor_barrier, 403 if inner_perm(peer,caller,'call')==false 'turned off calls'); on success broadcasts {type:'incoming_call', room, media, from:{handle,display_name,avatar_url}} to 'user:{peer_id}' and best-effort FCM push. POST /api/call/cancel {peer, room} — broadcasts {type:'call_cancelled', room, from} to 'user:{peer_id}' (404 if peer not found). POST /api/call/decline {peer, room} — broadcasts {type:'call_declined', room, from} to BOTH 'user:{peer_id}' AND dm_room(caller,peer) (404 if peer not found). POST /api/call/accept {peer, room} — broadcasts {type:'call_accepted', room, from} to 'user:{peer_id}' (404 if peer not found). TEST: register OWNER + MEMBER (adult DOB 1990-01-01), MEMBER accepts OWNER inner-circle invite. (1) MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:owner_handle, room:'r1', media:'video'} → 200 {ok:true}. (2) POST /api/call/ring {peer:owner_handle,...} with NO auth → 401. (3) POST /api/call/ring {peer:'nonexistenthandle', room:'r'} → 404. (4) MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:member_handle (self), room:'r'} → 400. (5) OWNER PUT /api/inner/{member_handle}/perms {call:false}; MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:owner_handle,room:'r'} → 403 'turned off calls'; restore call:true. (6) STRANGER (not connected) OWNER blocks STRANGER → STRANGER POST /api/call/ring {peer:owner_handle} → 403. (7) MEMBER POST /api/call/cancel {peer:owner_handle, room:'r'} → 200. (8) MEMBER POST /api/call/decline {peer:owner_handle, room:'r'} → 200. (9) MEMBER POST /api/call/accept {peer:owner_handle, room:'r'} → 200. (10) call/cancel|decline|accept with nonexistent peer → 404. NOTE: WebSocket delivery of the broadcast events is best verified in an integration/ws test but REST status codes + permission gating are the priority here."

  - task: "FCM push: device-token registration endpoints + guarded send helper"

        -comment: "NEW push token storage. POST /api/push/register {token, platform?} (auth) upserts db.device_tokens {user_id, token, platform, updated_at} (400 if empty token, 401 no auth). DELETE /api/push/register/{token} (auth) removes that token for the user. push_to_user() helper lazily inits firebase-admin from FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_JSON (inline) or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS (path); FAILS OPEN (no-op) when neither present or package missing — so preview works without the service account. dm_send now best-effort calls push_to_user(recipient, '#sender', preview, {url}) — no-op until service account configured. _purge_user cleans device_tokens. NOTE: actually SENDING pushes needs the Firebase service-account JSON (not yet provided) + firebase-admin in requirements. TEST: register user; POST /api/push/register {token:'test-fcm-tok-123', platform:'android'} → 200 {ok:true}; POST again same token → still 200 (idempotent upsert, no dup); POST {token:''} → 400; no-auth → 401; DELETE /api/push/register/test-fcm-tok-123 → 200; DM send regression: A→B inner-circle DM still 200 (push helper no-ops, no error)."
        -working: true
        -agent: "testing"
        -comment: "✅ ALL 7 FCM PUSH TOKEN REGISTRATION + DM PUSH HOOK TESTS PASSED (100% success). Comprehensive testing of NEW FCM push: device-token registration endpoints + guarded send helper completed with throwaway adult users (DOB 1990-01-01). Created test script /app/backend_test_fcm_push.py. TEST RESULTS: (1) REGISTER ADULT USER U (1/1 passed): Registered user U with DOB 1990-01-01 → 200 ✓. Adult user registration working correctly ✓. (2) TOKEN REGISTRATION (1/1 passed): U POST /api/push/register {token:'test-fcm-tok-123', platform:'android'} → 200 {ok:true} ✓. Token registered successfully ✓. (3) IDEMPOTENT UPSERT (1/1 passed): U POST /api/push/register {token:'test-fcm-tok-123', platform:'android'} again → 200 {ok:true} ✓. Idempotent upsert works (no duplicate error) ✓. Same token can be registered multiple times without errors ✓. (4) EMPTY TOKEN VALIDATION (1/1 passed): U POST /api/push/register {token:''} → 400 'Missing token' ✓. Empty token correctly rejected ✓. (5) AUTH ENFORCEMENT (1/1 passed): POST /api/push/register {token:'x'} with NO Authorization header → 401 'Missing Bearer token' ✓. Authentication correctly enforced ✓. (6) TOKEN UNREGISTRATION (1/1 passed): U DELETE /api/push/register/test-fcm-tok-123 → 200 {ok:true} ✓. Token unregistered successfully ✓. (7) REGRESSION - DM PUSH HOOK (1/1 passed): Registered users A and B (DOB 1990-01-01) ✓. A invites B to inner circle → 200 ✓. B accepts A's inner circle invite → 200 ✓. A POST /api/dms/{B_handle} {text:'hi from A'} → 200 ✓. DM sent successfully (push hook did NOT raise error even though firebase-admin is not installed and no service account is configured) ✓. B GET /api/dms/{A_handle} → message 'hi from A' present ✓. DM regression test passed (push hook fail-open behavior working correctly) ✓. NO ISSUES FOUND. FCM push token registration + guarded send helper feature is production-ready. All flows working correctly: (1) Token registration with proper validation (empty token → 400, no auth → 401), (2) Idempotent upsert (no duplicate errors), (3) Token unregistration, (4) Push hook in DM send does NOT break DMs even though FCM is unconfigured (fail-open behavior working correctly). The push_to_user() helper correctly fails open (no-op) when firebase-admin is not installed or service account is not configured, allowing the app to work without push notifications until the service account is provided."

  - task: "Disappearing (view-once) DM media"
    implemented: true

    status_history:

        -comment: "NEW view-once media. DMSend gains view_once bool (only honoured when media_url present). dm_send stores view_once + view_once_viewed=false; WS broadcast + response NEVER include media_url for view-once messages (wire_media=None). dm_history returns view-once messages with media_url=null always + flags view_once, view_once_viewed (so client shows placeholder). NEW POST /api/dms/{handle}/{message_id}/view: recipient-only one-time consume — 404 if missing, 403 if not a participant, 400 if not view_once, 403 if caller is the SENDER ('You can't reopen media you sent'), 410 if already viewed or url wiped; on success returns {media_url, media_type} ONCE, sets view_once_viewed=true + view_once_viewed_at, and WIPES media_url from db (true disappearing), broadcasts WS dm_viewed. Regression: normal (non-view-once) media messages unchanged (media_url present in history + response). TEST: A & B inner-circle. A sends {media_url:'https://x/p.jpg', media_type:'image', view_once:true}. (1) A dm_history → that msg has view_once=true, media_url=null (sender doesn't get url in history). (2) B dm_history → view_once=true, view_once_viewed=false, media_url=null. (3) B POST /view → 200 {media_url:'https://x/p.jpg'}. (4) B POST /view again → 410. (5) A (sender) POST /view on a fresh view-once msg → 403. (6) B dm_history after view → view_once_viewed=true. (7) non-participant → 403. Normal image send (view_once false/omitted) → history media_url present."
        -working: true
        -agent: "testing"

TEST RESULTS: (1) SEND VIEW-ONCE (1/1 passed): A POST /api/dms/{B_handle} {media_url:'https://example.com/p.jpg', media_type:'image', view_once:true} → 200 ✓. Response has view_once=true ✓. (2) SENDER HISTORY (1/1 passed): A GET /api/dms/{B_handle} → msg1 present with view_once=true, media_url=null ✓. Sender doesn't get URL in history ✓. (6) RECIPIENT HISTORY AFTER VIEW (1/1 passed): B GET /api/dms/{A_handle} → msg1 now view_once_viewed=true, media_url still null ✓. History never exposes URL even after viewing ✓. (7) SENDER RULE (1/1 passed): A sends ANOTHER view-once image to B (msg2=gif-troubleshoot-1) ✓. A POST /api/dms/{B_handle}/{msg2}/view → 403 with detail containing 'can't reopen' ✓. (9) ERROR PATHS (2/2 passed): B POST /api/dms/{A_handle}/nonexistentid/view → 404 ✓. A sends NORMAL text message to B (msg3=gif-troubleshoot-1) ✓. (10) REGRESSION (1/1 passed): A sends NORMAL image (POST /api/dms/{B_handle} {media_url:'https://example.com/normal.jpg', media_type:'image'} — view_once omitted) → 200 ✓. REGRESSION CHECK (1/1 passed): B GET /api/dms/{A_handle} still returns can_voice=True and can_call=True booleans ✓. Inner-Circle Voice/Call enforcement flags still present ✓. NO ISSUES FOUND. Disappearing (view-once) DM media feature is production-ready. All flows working correctly: (1) View-once messages withhold media_url from wire (response + WS broadcast), (2) dm_history returns view-once messages with media_url=null always + flags view_once/view_once_viewed, (3) POST /api/dms/{handle}/{message_id}/view returns URL exactly once to recipient (404 if missing, 403 if not participant, 400 if not view-once, 403 if sender tries to reopen, 410 if already viewed), (4) URL wiped from db after viewing (true disappearing), (5) Normal media messages unchanged (media_url present in history), (6) Inner-Circle Voice/Call flags regression confirmed."

agent_communication:
    -agent: "main"
    -message: "NEW FEATURES — INNER-CIRCLE NICKNAMES + CUSTOM STICKERS (backend only, do NOT test frontend). Register adults A and B (DOB 1990-01-01). (A) NICKNAMES: (1) A PUT /api/inner/{B_handle}/nickname {nickname:'Jinky'} BEFORE any inner relationship -> 403. (2) Establish inner: A POST /api/inner/invite/{B_handle}; B POST /api/inner/accept/{A_handle}. (3) A PUT /api/inner/{B_handle}/nickname {nickname:'Jinky'} -> 200. (4) A GET /api/inner -> the B entry has nickname='Jinky'. (5) A GET /api/dms/{B_handle} -> peer.nickname='Jinky' AND peer_is_inner=true. (6) A PUT /api/inner/{B_handle}/nickname {nickname:''} -> 200 (clears). (7) A PUT nickname with a banned slur -> 400. (8) no-auth -> 401. (B) STICKERS: (1) A GET /api/stickers -> []. (2) A POST /api/stickers {url:'https://example.com/s1.png'} -> 200 returns {id,url}. (3) A GET /api/stickers -> 1 item. (4) A DELETE /api/stickers/{id} -> 200; DELETE same id again -> 404. (5) A POST /api/stickers {url:''} -> 400. (6) Sticker send: A POST /api/dms/{B_handle} {media_url:'https://example.com/s1.png', media_type:'sticker'} -> 200 (inner circle so can_dm true). (7) no-auth on /api/stickers -> 401. Do NOT test frontend."
    -agent: "testing"

TEST RESULTS: (1) RING HAPPY PATH (1/1 passed): MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:OWNER_handle, room:'r1', media:'video'} → 200 {ok:true} ✓. Ring successful ✓. (3) NONEXISTENT PEER (1/1 passed): MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:'nosuchhandle123', room:'r'} → 404 ✓. Nonexistent peer correctly rejected ✓. (4) SELF-CALL (1/1 passed): MEMBER POST /api/call/ring {peer:MEMBER_handle (self), room:'r'} → 400 ✓. Self-call correctly rejected ✓. (5) CALL PERMISSION (1/1 passed): OWNER PUT /api/inner/{MEMBER_handle}/perms {call:false} → 200 ✓. All cancel/decline/accept correctly reject nonexistent peer ✓. (10) REGRESSION (1/1 passed): MEMBER POST /api/livekit/token {room:'r', peer:OWNER_handle} → 200 with participant_token ✓. LiveKit token endpoint still works correctly ✓. NO ISSUES FOUND. Call signaling (ringing) feature is production-ready. All flows working correctly: (A) Ring endpoint enforces all barriers (404 peer not found, 400 self-call, 401 no auth, 403 call permission turned off), (B) Cancel/decline/accept endpoints work correctly (200 on success, 404 for nonexistent peer), (C) Call permission toggle works (call:false blocks ring with 403, call:true allows ring), (D) LiveKit token endpoint regression confirmed (still works with peer parameter).     -agent: "main"
    -message: "Test (backend only) THREE new features. Adult users (DOB 1990-01-01). Admin admin@clanchat.app / ClanChatAdmin!2025. (A) EDIT HISTORY: A creates a PUBLIC post (POST /api/posts {tier:'public',text:'v1'}). PUT /api/posts/{id} {text:'v2'} then {text:'v3'}. GET /api/posts/{id}/history -> {current:{text:'v3'}, history:[{text:'v2'},{text:'v1'}]} (newest previous first). GET /api/posts/{id} in feed shows edited_count=2. Create a FOLLOWERS-tier post by A; a stranger (not follower) GET /api/posts/{id}/history -> 403. Wall: POST /api/wall/{A} {text:'w1'} by A, PUT /api/wall/{wid} {text:'w2'}, GET /api/wall/{wid}/history has history with 'w1'. (B) PIN: A creates 4 posts p1..p4. POST /api/posts/{p1}/pin,{p2}/pin,{p3}/pin -> 200 pinned=true; POST /api/posts/{p4}/pin -> 400 (max 3). GET /api/u/{A_handle} (public_profile) -> pinned_posts length 3, each pinned=true.     -agent: "testing"
    -message: "❌ CRITICAL BUG FOUND - Discussion Boards tier-based access control BROKEN. 31/33 tests passed (93.9% success, 2 CRITICAL security failures). Comprehensive testing completed with throwaway users. CRITICAL SECURITY VULNERABILITY: backend/server.py line 1156 in can_read_board() missing 'await' keyword causes tier-based access control to FAIL. Current code: `if viewer == owner or is_admin_user_id(viewer):` should be `if viewer == owner or await is_admin_user_id(viewer):`. The missing 'await' causes is_admin_user_id(viewer) to return a coroutine object (always truthy), making the condition ALWAYS TRUE for ANY user. This allows STRANGERS to access followers-tier boards and FOLLOWERS to access inner-tier boards. Verified: STRANGER (not a follower) can read followers-tier board with can_post=true. This is a SECURITY VULNERABILITY affecting ALL tier-based board access. FIX REQUIRED: Add 'await' before is_admin_user_id(viewer) on line 1156. All other features working correctly: banned-word filter (title/desc/post text/names all correctly rejected with 400), AI labels (generated/assisted/altered/none working, invalid defaults to 'none'), report categories (valid accepted, invalid rejected with 400), board CRUD operations, moderation (delete posts/boards). See status_history for detailed test results."
